classification: fixed agreement gate on C-sleeve candidates; original C score and all portfolio rules frozen

factor_definition.formula: rank each of momentum_60d, quality-value, cash-quality and low-vol cross-sectionally; count ranks above the 60th percentile; keep at least two

gold_proxy.rule: monthly close > 200-day MA uses gold; otherwise 50/50 treasury+dividend

hypothesis: Removing C-sleeve candidates that rank above the 60th percentile in fewer than two of four dimensions reduces single-factor extremes and broadens net-profit generation enough to improve 2022 and 5x concentration without degrading long-window return or drawdown.
limits: The gate is derived from the same four sleeves and is not an independent data source.
A 2-of-4 agreement threshold is a fixed economic rule, not an optimized parameter.
Financial firms are handled by existing C-sleeve filters rather than separate treatment.
Current-snapshot industry classification is backfilled through history.
Membership is reconstructed and ETF qfq is not official PIT total return.
The common window starts in 2022 because TTM financial factors are unavailable earlier.
The 10% C cap and gold trend rule were selected in prior post-hoc research.
Candidate breadth under the gate averages 76.5 names/day but has a minimum of 1, which can create concentration on sparse days.
